title: Control Flow in Templates
summary: Show, hide, repeat, and switch parts of your template.
heading: Control Flow in Templates

blocks.text: @if shows a block only when a condition is true, with an optional @else. It's the same idea as the if/else from Chapter 2, but inside the template.
Here it is as a live Angular example — press the button to flip the value and watch the block switch. Edit it and run:
@for renders a block once for each item in a list. The track part helps Angular update the list efficiently — usually track a unique id.

blocks.text: @empty is optional — it shows when the list has no items.
A live Angular example — add items and watch @for render each one. Edit it and run:

blocks.html:
@for (item of items; track item) {
  • {{ item }}
    • } @empty {
  • No items yet.
    • }

blocks.text: @switch picks one block out of several based on a value — handy when there are more than two options.

You may see older code using *ngIf and *ngFor as attributes. The newer @if and @for blocks are built into the template, easier to read, and the recommended choice today.

items: @for (item of list; track item.id) repeats a block.
